transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Well, what brought me in is... I just keep forgetting things at work. I do maintenance, and I keep missing scheduled callbacks, work orders, and even just basic follow-ups I promised people I'd get to. 

It's gotten pretty bad. The paperwork and missed calls have piled up so much that my job actually sent me here. They basically told me I need to get this figured out before I completely lose my shot at moving up.
Have you noticed any other changes besides forgetting things, like trouble focusing, finding the right words, or making decisions at work?

Yeah, focusing is definitely a big issue. Like, I can start looking at a digital work order, thinking I’ve got it figured out. But halfway through reading the notes, my mind just... slips off. I'll get distracted by the next noise in the building, or I start thinking about another job I have to do. Then I look back at the screen and realize I don’t even know what I just looked at.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

No, not really. I mean... I get frustrated, sure, because of the mistakes I keep making at work. But I wouldn't say I feel down or hopeless. I still enjoy my regular stuff when I'm off the clock. It's really just the focus and the forgetting that's messing me up right now.
Did you have similar issues with focus or forgetfulness when you were a child, like in school or completing tasks at home?

Yes, actually. I remember being this way back in grade school, long before I had any of this job pressure. My teachers always told my parents I was bright, but I was constantly misplacing my papers or missing parts of the directions. They always had to give me extra reminders just to get me to finish my classwork. So, yeah, it's been an issue for a long time.
Do you notice these focus and forgetfulness issues in other areas of your life, like at home or in social situations, or do they mostly happen at work?

It's everywhere, honestly. It's definitely worse at work because there are more consequences, but it happens at home all the time. I'll go into the kitchen to get a glass of water, see the mail on the counter, start sorting through that, and then thirty minutes later I realize I never got my water. Or my husband will ask me to pick up something from the store on my way home, and unless I write it down and stick it to my steering wheel, I'll completely forget. Even in conversations with friends, I find myself zoning out and missing half of what they said. So, yeah, it's not just a work thing.
When you think back to your childhood, did you start having trouble with focus and forgetfulness before age 12?

Yeah, definitely before I was 12. Like I said, I remember it happening back in grade school. I was probably around seven or eight when the teachers really started noticing that I wasn't finishing my work and was losing my assignments all the time. So it definitely started when I was pretty young.
Back when you were in grade school, did you have trouble focusing and forgetting things in different settings, like at home and in social situations, or was it mostly in school?

It was everywhere back then, too. I mean, school was where I got in trouble for it the most, but my parents were always getting frustrated with me at home. I'd forget to do my chores, or I'd start cleaning my room and get distracted by a toy or a book and never finish. Even playing with other kids, I'd sometimes just... zone out or lose track of the rules of the game we were playing. So, yeah, it wasn't just a school thing when I was a kid either.
Back when you were in grade school, did these focus and forgetfulness issues significantly interfere with your schoolwork or relationships with your family or friends?

Yeah, it really did. I mean, like I just said, I was always getting in trouble at school for losing my assignments and not finishing things, so that definitely made schoolwork hard. And at home, my parents were just constantly frustrated with me for forgetting my chores or getting distracted. It caused a lot of friction with them. I don't really have much else to add to it, but yeah, it definitely got in the way of things back then.
As an adult, do you experience symptoms of hyperactivity or impulsivity, such as feeling restless, having trouble staying seated, interrupting others, or acting without thinking?

No, not really. I mean, I don't feel restless or have trouble sitting still or anything like that. I'm usually pretty quiet, so I don't interrupt people or just blurt things out. It's really just the focusing and the forgetting that gives me a hard time. I don't really have those other issues you mentioned.
